newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian police make arrests after protests.
newsitem.headline: Albanian police make arrests after protests.

text.p: The Albanian government said on Wednesday it had arrested a considerable number of people across the country following violent demonstrations sparked by the collapse of get-rich-quick pyramid investment schemes.

"In the districts where destruction and burning down of state institutions have taken place, the police have stopped and accompanied to the police stations a considerable number of citizens," the interior ministry said in a statement. It did not say precisely how many people had been detained.
Rioting erupted throughout this poor Balkan state last weekend with many investors fearing for their life savings and blaming the government for the failure of the private schemes.

"The detention of these citizens...is totally based on facts, witnesses and incontestable proofs, which testify that these citizens have encouraged, organised and executed the violent actions," the interior ministry said.

Earlier on Wednesday President Sali Berisha said investors caught up in the investment scams might not be fully compensated. Hours later police broke up an anti-government rally in Tirana organised by Hazem Hajdari, one of the leaders of a 1990 revolt which toppled the former communist regime.

The interior ministry said Wednesday's arrests had nothing to do with politics. "Not in a single case has their detentions been due to the party affiliations that some of them may have," the statement said.
